title: The concrete balanced tensor presheaf
statement: For a commutative condensed ring R, a profinite group P and a closed subgroup H, the concrete finite-sum quotients of [def-sfb-condensed-tensor-induction-data] form a TensorInductionPresheaf R P H, including the section identifications and every specified restriction, functor-map, left-action and naturality formula. The finite-sum quotient also has the semilinear balanced universal property: every additive, semilinear-in-m balanced family v(p,m) admits a unique semilinear quotient map, and maps from the quotient agree if they agree on pure tensors.

source.place: Agent-formulated induction argument below paragraph (3); The concrete balanced tensor presheaf. External reference WANTED, as for the parent.

proof.text: The quotient symbols are additive and scalar-linear in the module variable and satisfy balancing: each difference is one of the spanning relations.

For a semilinear family v(p,m) satisfying these three relations, sum sigma(a)v(p,m) on finite formal sums and descend through the quotient. The spanning relations are in the kernel. Maps from the quotient agree if they agree on pure symbols, by linearity of finite sums.

Apply the quotient map to restriction of coefficients, precomposition of p and restriction of m. Naturality of the action preserves balancing. Check identity and composition on generators. Equivariant module morphisms act on the second variable; equivariance preserves balancing, and naturality and functor laws hold on generators.

Left multiplication of the first variable preserves balancing by associativity and gives linear endomorphisms. The monoid laws and compatibility with restrictions hold on generators, hence on all quotient sections. Package these constructions with identity section isomorphisms.
